1.explanation:
• architecture.md – Gives an overview of how Lighthouse audits are wired together, so you can trace from the report UI back to the audit implementation.
• new-audits.md – Shows how an audit defines its numeric results and the displayValue property; this is where the `.toFixed` or formatting would be applied.
• understanding-results.md – Describes how the JSON results get translated into the report UI and how displayValue should appear, helping you find where to strip off ‘.0’.
• scoring.md – Although mostly about scoring, it explains numeric thresholds and formatting conventions which the DOM-size audit follows.
• readme.md – Provides entry-point documentation and conventions for editing the Lighthouse docs and tying changes back to the core codebase.
• plugins.md – Illustrates how plugin audits format and report numeric values, useful as a reference for the correct way to format integer-only metrics.
1.bug_scenario: The DOM-size audit in the Lighthouse report is showing its three statistics (Total DOM Elements, Maximum DOM Depth, and Maximum Child Elements) with a trailing “.0” (e.g. “2,008.0” rather than “2,008”). Since these counts will always be whole numbers, the extra precision is unnecessary and should be removed.
